```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 3.94)
library(manimR)
```

manimR ports [Manim Community](https://www.manim.community/) to R. This
vignette shows the main ideas: mobjects, scenes, animations and rendering.

## Mobjects

A mobject is anything that can be drawn. Constructors mirror Manim, and every
method that changes a mobject returns it, so calls chain with `$`:

```{r mobjects}
circle <- Circle(radius = 1.5, color = BLUE)$set_fill(BLUE, opacity = 0.3)
square <- Square(side_length = 2, color = YELLOW)$next_to(circle, RIGHT, buff = 0.5)
label <- Text("shapes", font_size = 36)$next_to(VGroup(circle, square), DOWN)
plot(VGroup(circle, square, label))
```

Points live in `mob$points`, an n x 3 matrix of cubic Bezier control points
(four rows per curve), exactly as in Manim.

## Scenes and animations

A scene is an R6 class that inherits from `Scene` and defines `construct()`.
Inside, `self$play()` runs animations and `self$wait()` pauses.

```{r scene, eval = FALSE}
Pythagoras <- R6::R6Class("Pythagoras", inherit = Scene,
  public = list(construct = function() {
    eq <- MathTex("a^2", "+", "b^2", "=", "c^2")
    self$play(Write(eq))
    self$play(eq[5]$animate$set_color(YELLOW))
    tracker <- ValueTracker(0)
    number <- DecimalNumber(0)$next_to(eq, DOWN)
    number$add_updater(function(m) m$set_value(tracker$get_value()))
    self$add(number)
    self$play(tracker$animate$set_value(25), run_time = 2)
    self$wait()
  })
)
render(Pythagoras, quality = "l", preview = TRUE)
```

The `$animate` builder turns any sequence of method calls into an animation,
and updaters (`add_updater()`) run every frame.

## Rendering

`render()` writes `media/videos/<module>/<quality>/<Scene>.mp4`. Use
`quality = "l"` while drafting and `"h"` or `"k"` for final output.
`format = "gif"` produces an animated GIF and `save_last_frame = TRUE` also
writes the final frame as a PNG. `render_file()` renders scenes defined in a
script, and the RStudio addins do the same for the active editor.

## Checking against Manim

The test suite compares manimR's geometry, alignment, transforms, rate
functions and LaTeX output with values dumped from Python manim, so scenes
look the same in both.
